phrases.latin: Tum, quod cotīdiē fit nec umquam sine certāmine, faciēs lavanda erat, dentēs pūrgandī.
phrases.english: Then came what happens every day and never without a fight: washing the face and brushing the teeth.

phrases.latin: id perfēcit quod puer coeperat, fricāns ubi ille lamberat. «Ōs aperī. Lātius. Jam ēlue. Exspue. Satis est.»
phrases.english: he finished what the boy had begun, brushing where he had only licked. “Open your mouth. Wider. Now rinse. Spit. That’s enough.”

sources: Lewis & Short: frico · Lewis & Short: eluo · Mir: morning routine (transcription)
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 36, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).
